title: VIVID: Backbone Training-Free Text-to-Image Video Editing via Variational Latent Anchors

problem.claim: Backbone training-free text-to-image video editing requires cross-frame latent selection that supports spatiotemporal coherence during denoising.

gap.claim: Existing static heuristic keyframe policies and temperature-softmax responsibilities are numerically sensitive, scale-biased, and less generalizable across diverse scenes.

contributions.claim: VIVID is an uncertainty-aware variational latent anchoring module that dynamically selects informative frames and compresses cross-frame latents into semantic anchors.
VIVID learns latent assignments with a variational objective combining contrastive alignment and prior regularization to preserve spatial details and temporal continuity.
VIVID is designed as a drop-in replacement for heuristic selection in existing backbone training-free text-to-image video editing frameworks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on standard benchmarks and in-the-wild videos demonstrate state-of-the-art inversion fidelity, editing quality, and temporal consistency.
The authors report reduced memory and runtime compared with prior backbone training-free baselines.
Code is reported as released at the supplied GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Backbone training-free video editing enables lightweight prompt-driven edits using pretrained text-to-image diffusion models.
Cross-frame latent selection during DDIM inversion is identified as a key determinant of later spatiotemporal coherence.
Existing static and temperature-softmax selection strategies suffer from numerical sensitivity, scale bias, and degraded generalization.
VIVID dynamically selects informative frames and forms variational semantic anchors with regularized stable assignments.
The authors report benchmark and in-the-wild improvements in fidelity, editing quality, temporal consistency, memory, and runtime.

source_observation.claim: Cross-frame latent selection can substantially affect spatiotemporal coherence in diffusion-based video editing.

interpretation.claim: Latent selection should be treated as a central modeling decision rather than a fixed preprocessing heuristic.

application.claim: For related video-generation or editing systems, evaluate adaptive frame or latent selection jointly with temporal consistency.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported approach transfers beyond the described backbone training-free text-to-image video editing setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not provide details of the variational objective, contrastive alignment, or prior regularization.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported performance or efficiency claims.
